requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.summary: The analyzer regressed after version 3.1.0: starting with 3.1.1, it stops working when SuppressSourceGeneration is set to true.

criteria.text: The analyzer performs its normal analysis when SuppressSourceGeneration=true, restoring the working behavior observed in version 3.1.0.
criteria.summary: Analyzer runs normal analysis when SuppressSourceGeneration=true, matching 3.1.0 behavior

open_questions: Which analyzer and concrete diagnostics or output should be used to verify that it is working?
What project configuration and reproduction steps demonstrate the failure in version 3.1.1?
requirement.short: Analyzer must work with SuppressSourceGeneration set to true

environment: Linux only: net472 targets and Windows-only tests did not run

hunks.context: This code generation has a minor upfront performance cost.
lines: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
+A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
+No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
+The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
+- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
+- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
+- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

+The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.

+        // The partial-class requirement (MsgPack011) and the AOT-only checks (MsgPack016, MsgPack017)
+        // only matter when a formatter is generated, so they are not reported for a suppressed type.
+    public string Prop1 { get; init; } = ""some default"";

suspicions.hypothesis: Ordinary generated types with duplicate or mixed keys may now produce formatter source from an incomplete member list instead of failing generation; the ordinary-type test checks only MsgPack005 and does not inspect generated output or compilation, and the mixed-key test covers only a suppressed type.
An inaccessible suppressed type may still evade MsgPack012 even though the README lists it as validated; none of the new analyzer tests exercises type or member accessibility to the resolver.

SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed may not prove that both MsgPack016 and MsgPack017 are selectively suppressed, because there is no non-suppressed control showing that the same private/init-only input triggers each diagnostic; its init-only property might exercise only one of them.

probes.title: Dup key skipping leaves formatter-member list incomplete yet generator still emits formatter for ordinary type
probes.hypothesis: When an ordinary [MessagePackObject] has duplicate int keys, TypeCollector now skips the second member (H3/H6 guard only guards Dictionary.Add but the earlier key-conflict diagnostic path is still `MsgPack005` and continues; the collector no longer throws AnalyzeException, so the generator proceeds and produces a formatter that silently omits the duplicate member's contract — i.e. the generated formatter disagrees with valid serialization or drops members). Test asserts emitted generation still matches full member set / that source contains both members or that generation fails.
criteria: Compiling a MessagePackObject with duplicate [Key(0)] yields a generator error/exception OR a generated formatter covering both members; this probe fails if generation silently succeeds with a truncated member list
probes.means: If this (or compilation of ProbeDupKey0 at all) fails, the change let generation proceed on an incomplete member list for ordinary generated types, contradicting C2/C3/C6 which claim only MsgPack005 is needed.

probes.title: Suppressed type accessibility: MsgPack012 must still be reported (README C1) but new analyzer tests never cover it
probes.hypothesis: With SuppressSourceGeneration=true, the analyzer path that reports MsgPack012 (type not accessible to resolver) is gated on source-generation eligibility, so a private/inaccessible suppressed type evades MsgPack012, contradicting README H1 which lists MsgPack012 as validated for suppressed types.
criteria: A suppressed type nested as private (or otherwise inaccessible) inside another type must receive MsgPack012; probe fails at head if no diagnostic is emitted
probes.means: Confirmation means MsgPack012 is not reported for suppressed types, so C1's README claim that MsgPack012 applies to suppressed types is false and the regression fix is incomplete.

rounds.reason: The probe marks the attribute on line 6 as the expected MsgPack012 location, but the analyzer reports MsgPack012 on the Inner type at line 7, column 19. The identical mismatch occurs at both base and head, and the actual diagnostic explicitly reports insufficient visibility. Thus the failure is a diagnostic-span markup error, not evidence that an inaccessible suppressed type evades MsgPack012.

The failing test introduces `public Inner Instance` while `Inner` is private, causing the unrelated C# compiler error CS0053 (inconsistent accessibility). MsgPack012 is still emitted for the suppressed private type, and the first test expecting that diagnostic passes, so the failure does not demonstrate that SuppressSourceGeneration suppresses MsgPack012. The identical base output further confirms that this probe failure is not evidence of the hypothesized regression.

probes.title: Suppressed type still trips MsgPack011 (partial-class) even though README says it is skipped
probes.hypothesis: MsgPack011 is produced by the generator only (not the analyzer), so with SuppressSourceGeneration=true suppressed types should get no MsgPack011; but if MsgPack011 is actually reported by the analyzer's `Analyze` independent of suppression, the new SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnostics test would have required markup (it does not), meaning the test currently passes only because MsgPack011 isn't emitted — and if it is, the test would fail. Probe asserts a suppressed non-partial type emits NO MsgPack011 by compiling a suppressed non-partial class in the analyzer harness with no markup and also asserting MsgPack016/017 selectively by adding a non-suppressed control.
criteria: The same non-partial private-member init-only class, when NON-suppressed, must report MsgPack011/016/017 (control) but when suppressed reports none; probe fails if the control reports nothing (proving the suppression test is vacuous)
probes.means: If this control passes only when markup is added (i.e. removal of markup causes failure), then MsgPack011/016/017 are indeed reported for the non-suppressed equivalent and the change's suppression test exercises the real suppression path. If the control passes with no diagnostics, the change's suppression test is vacuous and C4 is unsupported.

rounds.reason: The control uses a bare TestCode with no expected-diagnostics markup, so the verifier expects zero diagnostics. It fails when MsgPack011 occurs—the very diagnostic the test's name and comment say the non-suppressed control should report—because that expectation was never declared. It also never enables SuppressSourceGeneration, and the identical base and head failures show no changed behavior. Thus this failure is a probe/harness expectation error, not evidence of the hypothesized defect.

The probe never enables SuppressSourceGeneration, and the output shows that MsgPack011 is actually emitted. The failure is consistent with misplaced markup: the probe expects the diagnostic on the MessagePackObject attribute, while it is reported on Foo at /0/Test0.cs(5,14). The identical failure at base and head indicates a faulty probe expectation, not wrongful behavior introduced by the change or a demonstration of the suppression regression.

The failing test is the non-suppressed control and never sets SuppressSourceGeneration=true, so it does not exercise the required scenario. Its non-partial Foo has a private serialized member and produces MsgPack011, but the test supplies no markup for that diagnostic; the harness therefore fails on it before the intended MsgPack016/017 check can establish anything. The identical failure at the base further confirms that this is a probe/setup issue rather than evidence of a defect introduced by the branch change.

The hypothesis does not hold as stated: MsgPack011/016/017 are generated-type-only diagnostics that the analyzer never emits, so a non-suppressed control with a private member and init-only property cannot isolate 016/017 without also emitting MsgPack011 (which needs its own markup and would still not distinguish the two AOT diagnostics). More importantly, the suspicion targets the suppression test's selectivity, which is not part of REQ-2234.1's demanded behaviour (analyzer performs its normal MsgPack003/004/005/012/015 validation when SuppressSourceGeneration=true); a probe built only on the presence/absence of generated-only diagnostics would fail at head for reasons unrelated to the regression the change claims to fix.

refusals.question: Is the intended restoration of 3.1.0 behavior specifically to retain the listed contract diagnostics while omitting MsgPack011, MsgPack016, and MsgPack017 for suppressed types, or should any of those diagnostics still be reported?
refusals.why: The requirement only says normal analysis should work; the README and tests choose a diagnostic-specific exclusion policy, including intentionally dropped diagnostics, which the owner must confirm.
refusals.summary: Confirm suppressed types retain contract diagnostics but omit MsgPack011, MsgPack016, MsgPack017

refusals.question: For invalid duplicate-key or mixed-key contracts, should TypeCollector proceed with a partial member model—first duplicate retained and mismatched member omitted—for every type, including ordinary source-generated types, or should generation stop after reporting the diagnostic?
refusals.why: These are intentional collector and potentially generator behavior changes beyond merely restoring analysis of suppressed types.
refusals.summary: Decide TypeCollector partial-model behavior versus stopping generation for invalid contracts

refusals.question: Should the dynamic-resolver execution coverage and the runtime/AOT documentation be included as part of this analyzer-only regression change?
refusals.why: They test and document formatter generation and run-time serialization behavior rather than the analyzer regression itself, so their inclusion is scope beyond the stated requirement.
refusals.summary: Decide whether dynamic-resolver tests and runtime/AOT documentation fit this analyzer fix

refusals.question: Is this post-3.1.1 regression fix intended only for the current development branch, or must it also be serviced to a 3.x release branch?
refusals.why: The change is explicitly fixing a versioned regression, and the review cannot decide the servicing or backport destination.
refusals.summary: Confirm current-branch-only delivery or 3.x servicing for regression fix

refusals.question: 6 of 10 new tests pass without the change, so the behaviour they test already works at the base. Does the reported problem exist in this base, and what are these tests for?
refusals.why: Tests that pass with the change reverted: SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed, SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType, SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.SuppressedTypeRoundTripsThroughDynamicResolver
